mainTopic: Where do we learn that we may follow a majority that is not in front of us (רובא דליתא קמן)? Proofs from the goats of יום כיפור, striking a father, a murderer, עדים זוממין, and שחיטה itself.
overview: This amud brings several proofs that the תורה relies on a majority we cannot see in front of us. It begins by finishing the proof from the goats of יום כיפור: the goat for עזאזל is never checked for being a טריפה, the lottery only works on a goat fit for ה׳, and the goat falls apart on the way down, so we must rely on the majority. רב מרי proves it from the death penalty for striking a father, since fatherhood rests on רוב בעילות אחר הבעל, even when the parents were in prison. רב כהנא proves it from executing a murderer, though the victim might have been a טרפה; we cannot examine the body, and even if we did, the sword wound could hide an earlier hole. רבינא proves it from עדים זוממין, who are executed only when their target is still alive, so there is no body to check. רב אשי proves it from שחיטה itself, since the cut wipes out the very spot where a hole might have been. That last proof is pushed back: maybe we rely on the majority only where checking is impossible, and even רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority, must eat meat. The amud ends with a suggestion that רבי מאיר really does avoid meat, which the גמרא answers on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the proof from the two goats of יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: The goats of יום כיפור are not checked for being a טריפה. So we must be relying on the rule that most animals are not טריפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe one of them, the goat for עזאזל, is a טריפה? Rather, isn't it because we say: follow the majority?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that started just before this line. The goat sent to עזאזל is never checked, so how do we know it is not a טריפה? The only answer is that we follow the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat for עזאזל is pushed off a cliff alive, so nobody ever checks its insides. If the הלכה still treats it as a kosher, valid animal, it must be relying on the fact that most animals are healthy. This is a majority we cannot see or count in front of us.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, which makes it unfit for eating or for a קרבן
Go after the majority: decide an unknown case based on what is usually true
Rather, isn't it...? This phrase introduces the only reasonable explanation, which is the point being proven

phrases.english: Perhaps one of them is a tereifa?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the two goats of יום כיפור from the line before. The worry is mainly about the goat for עזאזל, which is never checked.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not because we say:
Follow the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן זִיל בָּתַר רוּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation from the goats of יום כיפור that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That we may rely on a majority that is not in front of us
steps.raayaSupportSource: The goat for עזאזל is never checked, yet it is treated as valid

steps.title: Maybe it does not matter if the goat is a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: Someone might try to reject the proof by saying it makes no difference whether the goat for עזאזל is a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: what difference does it make to us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a possible way to knock down the proof. Maybe it simply does not matter if the goat for עזאזל is a טריפה, since it is not eaten or brought on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being a טריפה makes no difference for this goat, then there was never any doubt that needed solving. In that case the goat proves nothing about following the majority. The גמרא raises this objection only so it can answer it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a possible objection that the גמרא will answer
What practical difference does it make to us?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא, מַאי נָפְקָא לַן מִינַּהּ?
phrases.english: And if you would say: what difference does it make to us?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מַאי נָפְקָא לַן מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a possible reason why the proof in step 1 fails.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the goat for עזאזל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Maybe a טריפה goat for עזאזל is acceptable anyway, so there is no doubt to resolve

steps.title: The lottery only works on a goat fit for a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: It does matter, because the lottery only picks a goat for עזאזל out of animals that are fit to be offered to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the lottery only selects a goat for עזאזל when it is an animal fit to be offered to ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. The lottery only works on goats that are fit to be a קרבן, so a טריפה goat would ruin it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both goats have to be fit for ה׳ at the moment of the lottery, because either one could be picked for ה׳. A טריפה is not fit for a קרבן. So the doubt is real, and the proof from the majority still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The lottery that decides which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל
Establishes or designates
The place in the wilderness where the שעיר המשתלח is sent
Fit to be offered to ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the goat for עזאזל gets a pass because it is not burned on the מזבח. The lottery only works if both goats could have been chosen for ה׳.

phrases.english: But the lot does not determine a goat for Azazel
except for something fit to be offered to the Lord.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֵין גּוֹרָל קוֹבֵעַ לַעֲזָאזֵל אֶלָּא בְּדָבָר הָרָאוּי לַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the objection of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a halachic rule that shows the doubt really matters
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טריפה goat for עזאזל makes no difference
steps.terutzMaskana: A טריפה would make the lottery invalid, so we must be relying on the majority

steps.title: Maybe we check the goat afterward
steps.stepSummary: A second escape: maybe we do not rely on the majority, because we check the goat after it is thrown off the cliff.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that we check it afterward...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second possible way out of the proof. Maybe the goat is checked after it dies, so we never need to rely on the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goat's body were checked after the fall, any doubt about it being a טריפה would be cleared up for certain. Then there would be no proof that we follow a majority. This line sets up the answer that comes right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: We examine or check

phrases.english: And if you would say that we examine it,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּבָדְקִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 answered the first escape, this offers a new escape.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the goat for עזאזל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Maybe the goat is checked after death, so no majority is needed

steps.title: The goat falls apart, so it cannot be checked
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that the goat is torn limb from limb before it even gets halfway down the mountain, so checking it is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: it did not reach halfway down the mountain before it became torn limb from limb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second escape from a משנה. The goat is torn to pieces on the way down, so nobody can check it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A body torn into pieces cannot be properly checked for the signs of a טריפה. So there was never any way to clear up the doubt for certain. The הלכה must be relying on the majority, and the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Halfway down the mountain
Limb by limb, torn into pieces

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the goats of יום כיפור holds up. A טריפה would make the lottery invalid, and the goat can never be checked, so we must be relying on the majority of animals.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: לֹא הָיָה מַגִּיעַ לְמַחֲצִית הֶהָר
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: it did not reach halfway down the mountain
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת יומא.

phrases.english: before it became limbs upon limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן לֹא הָיָה מַגִּיעַ לְמַחֲצִית הֶהָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the escape of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A משנה shows the suggestion cannot work in reality
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The goat is checked after it dies
steps.terutzMaskana: Checking is impossible, so the הלכה relies on the majority

steps.title: רב מרי's proof from someone who strikes his father
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי proves the rule from the death penalty for striking a parent. We only know who the father is because most relations of a married woman are with her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: we learn it from someone who strikes his father or mother, whom the תורה says to execute. But we should worry that maybe this is not really his father! Rather, isn't it because we say: follow the majority, and most relations are with the husband?
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי offers a new, separate proof for following the majority. The תורה executes someone who strikes his father, even though we never know for certain that this man is his real father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no way to know for sure who a person's biological father is. The תורה still punishes with death, which is the most serious kind of case. That shows we rely on the majority: most of a married woman's relations are with her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from, meaning it is learned from
One who strikes his father or mother, which carries the death penalty
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Most relations of a married woman are with her husband

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis for treating a husband as the father of his wife's children. It applies even in capital cases.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
It is derived from one who strikes his father or his mother,
whom the Merciful One said to kill,
but let us be concerned: perhaps he is not his father?
Rather, is it not because we say:
Follow the majority,
and most acts of intercourse are attributable to the husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָרִי אָמַר אָתְיָא מִמַּכֵּה אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, independent source for the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: That we may rely on a majority that is not in front of us
steps.raayaSupportSource: The death penalty for striking a father, which depends on the majority rule for fatherhood

steps.title: Maybe the parents were locked in prison together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know this case depends on the majority. Maybe it is talking about parents locked in prison together, so the father is known for certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Maybe it is a case where his father and mother were locked up together in prison!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מרי's proof. Maybe the תורה's case is one where fatherhood is certain, so it says nothing about following a majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the parents were locked away together with no one else around, we would seem to know for sure who the father is. Then the death penalty would rest on certainty, not on the majority, and the proof would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this? This challenges an assumption
Locked up, imprisoned
Prison

phrases.english: From where do you know? Perhaps it is a case where
his father and mother were imprisoned in jail!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דִּלְמָא כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיוּ אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ חֲבוּשִׁים בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרי's proof from striking a father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse could be talking about a case where fatherhood is certain, so it would not depend on the majority

steps.title: No one can fully guard against forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: Even in prison, fatherhood is not certain, because no guard can fully prevent forbidden relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, there is no guardian against forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even the prison case does not give certainty. So fatherhood always depends on the majority, and רב מרי's proof stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No guard can fully prevent forbidden relations. So even when the parents were locked up together, we cannot be completely sure who the father is. Every case of striking a father must therefore rely on the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
There is no guardian that can prevent forbidden relations

steps.whatToRemember: רב מרי proves the rule of following the majority from the death penalty for striking a father. Fatherhood is never certain, not even in prison, so it always rests on רוב בעילות אחר הבעל.

phrases.english: Even so, there is no guardian for forbidden relations.
phrases.notes: Literally a 'steward' or guard: no amount of guarding can fully stop forbidden relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי אֵין אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס לַעֲרָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the suggested case still does not give certainty
steps.terutzMaskana: Fatherhood is never certain, so it always relies on the majority

steps.title: Proof from executing a murderer
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא proves we follow the majority. The תורה executes a murderer even though his victim might have been a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: We learn it from a murderer. The תורה says to kill him. But shouldn't we worry that maybe the victim was a טרפה? It must be because we say: follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב כהנא, brings his own proof that the תורה relies on the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who kills a טרפה is not executed. So if we were truly unsure about the victim, we could never execute the murderer. Since the תורה does command it, we must be assuming the victim was healthy, like most people are.

keyTerms.meaning: A murderer, one who kills a person
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Someone with a fatal wound or condition who is expected to die
Go after the majority

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
It is learned from one who kills a person,
about whom the Torah says: Kill him.
But let us worry: maybe the victim was a tereifa?
phrases.notes: The worry is that killing a טרפה does not bring the death penalty, so the murderer could not be executed.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not because we say:
Follow the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: אָתְיָא מֵהוֹרֵג אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof for the same rule, after רב מרי's proof from striking a parent
steps.raayaObject: That the תורה relies on the majority
steps.raayaSupportSource: The death penalty for a murderer, even though the victim might have been a טרפה

steps.title: Maybe we examine the victim's body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to escape the proof by suggesting we check the body to see whether the victim was a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that we examine him...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב כהנא's proof. Maybe we never rely on the majority, because we can check the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the body can be examined, there is no doubt left, and no need for a majority rule. This would make the proof fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible objection)
We examine, we check

phrases.english: And if you say that we examine him,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּבָדְקִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof in step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב כהנא's proof from the murderer
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Maybe the doubt can be removed by examining the body, so no majority is needed

steps.title: Examining would disgrace the body
steps.stepSummary: We cannot examine the body, because cutting it open would disgrace the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he would be disgraced!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we would not cut open the body to check, because that would disgrace the dead person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we do not examine, the doubt about a טרפה remains. Executing the murderer anyway shows we rely on the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Is disgraced, mutilated (from נִיווּל, disgracing a body)

phrases.english: But he would be disgraced!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מִינַּוַּול
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the escape in step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical barrier: the check is not allowed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could check the victim's body
steps.terutzMaskana: Checking would disgrace the dead, so we do not do it

steps.title: Maybe we disgrace the body to save the murderer's life
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that saving the murderer from a possibly wrong execution is worth disgracing the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that because of the loss of this man's life, we should disgrace the body...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the escape again. A life is at stake, so maybe we would allow examining the body after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The murderer's life is on the line. Preventing a wrongful execution might outweigh the honor of the dead, so perhaps we would examine the body after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Loss of a life
Let us disgrace it (cut open the body)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם אִיבּוּד נְשָׁמָה דְּהַאי –
phrases.english: And if you say that because of the loss of life of this one,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the murderer, who might be executed wrongly.

phrases.english: we should disgrace the body,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם אִיבּוּד נְשָׁמָה דְּהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the answer in step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that we would not examine the body
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Saving a life might justify disgracing the body

steps.title: The sword wound could hide an earlier hole
steps.stepSummary: Even if we examine the body, the fatal hole might have been right where the sword went in, so the doubt remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that maybe there was a hole right where the sword struck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that examining the body still would not remove the doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole that made the victim a טרפה could have been exactly where the sword wound is now, so we could never see it. Since the doubt can never be fully removed, executing the murderer must rely on the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us be concerned
Sword
A hole or perforation (one that can make a body a טרפה)

steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא's proof stands. A murderer is executed even though we can never be fully sure the victim was not a טרפה, so the תורה relies on the majority.

phrases.english: still, let us worry that perhaps
there was a hole in the place of the sword.
phrases.notes: The sword wound would cover up any hole that was already there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא בִּמְקוֹם סַיִיף נֶקֶב הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 and saves the proof in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Even the check cannot fully settle the doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Examining the body would show whether the victim was a טרפה
steps.terutzMaskana: The sword wound may hide the hole, so we still rely on the majority

steps.title: Proof from עדים זוממין
steps.stepSummary: רבינא proves we follow the majority. עדים זוממין are punished even though the man they testified against might have been a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We learn it from עדים זוממין. The תורה says, "You shall do to him as he plotted." But shouldn't we worry that maybe the man they testified against was a טרפה? It must be because we say: follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא, רבינא, brings another proof that the תורה relies on the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses who were caught lying about a capital crime get the death penalty they tried to bring on him. If he was a טרפה, their plot would not have been murder, so they should not be executed. Since the תורה still executes them, it must assume he was healthy, like most people.

keyTerms.meaning: Plotting witnesses, false witnesses proven to have been elsewhere at the time
As he plotted, the punishment he tried to cause
They testified

phrases.english: Ravina said:
It is learned from plotting witnesses,
about whom the Torah says:
"And you shall do to him as he plotted, etc."
But let us worry that maybe
the one they testified against was a tereifa?
Rather, is it not because we say:
Follow the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: אָתְיָא מֵעֵדִים זוֹמְמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another new proof for the same rule, after רב כהנא's
steps.raayaObject: That the תורה relies on the majority
steps.raayaSupportSource: The death penalty for עדים זוממין, even though their target might have been a טרפה

steps.title: Maybe we examine the man who was executed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again suggests we could check the man's body and so avoid relying on the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that we examine him...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the same escape against רבינא's proof. Maybe the man was executed and his body can be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the false testimony already led to his execution. If so, his body could be checked for a fatal condition, and no majority would be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Him, here the man the witnesses testified against

phrases.english: And if you say that we examine him,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּבָדְקִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof in step 14
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Maybe the victim's body can be checked, so there is no doubt

steps.title: Witnesses are executed only if the man was not killed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that עדים זוממין are executed only if their target was not killed, so there is no body to check.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: ברבי says: If they did not kill him, they are executed. If they did kill him, they are not executed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the escape with a ברייתא. False witnesses are executed only when the man they testified against was not killed, so there is never a body to check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses are only executed when the man they lied about is still alive. A living man cannot be cut open and checked, so the doubt about a טרפה remains. Executing the witnesses must therefore rely on the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: A distinguished sage, one of the great ones
They killed, meaning their testimony already led to his execution
They are executed

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but it is the rule: עדים זוממין are executed only if their target was NOT killed. That is why there is never a body to examine.

phrases.english: But it was taught: A distinguished sage says:
If they did not kill him, they are executed;
phrases.notes: "Kill" here means their testimony got the man executed.

phrases.english: if they killed him, they are not executed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: בְּרַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָרְגוּ – נֶהֱרָגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 and protects the proof in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: A source shows the suggested check is impossible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The executed man's body could be checked
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses are executed only when the man is still alive, so no body exists to check

steps.title: Proof for following the majority from slaughter itself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proves we follow the רוב, because the תורה allows us to slaughter and eat even though the knife may have cut through a hole that would make the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We learn it from שחיטה itself. The תורה says 'slaughter and eat.' But we should worry that maybe he slaughtered right in the spot of a hole! It must be because we say: follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a new proof that we follow the רוב, this time from the basic law of שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole in the windpipe or food pipe makes an animal a טרפה. The שחיטה cut goes right through that area, so any hole there is wiped out and can never be checked. Since the תורה still lets us eat, it must be relying on the fact that most animals are not טרפות.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher slaughter of an animal
A hole (here, in the windpipe or food pipe), which makes the animal a טרפה
Go after the majority; follow what is usually true
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אָתְיָא מִשְּׁחִיטָה עַצְמָהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It comes from slaughter itself,
for the Merciful One said: Slaughter and eat,
phrases.notes: A short way of saying the תורה allows slaughtering and eating meat (דברים 12:21).

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא בִּמְקוֹם נֶקֶב קָא שָׁחֵיט?
phrases.english: but let us worry that perhaps he is slaughtering right in the place of a hole?
Rather, is it not because we say:
Go after the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אָתְיָא מִשְּׁחִיטָה עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate proof for the רוב, after the עדים זוממין proof in steps 14-16.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that we follow the majority (זיל בתר רובא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תורה's permission to slaughter and eat, even though the cut destroys any chance of checking for a hole at that spot.

steps.title: Maybe we rely on the majority only when checking is impossible
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא (or רב שימי) answers that שחיטה only proves we follow the רוב where we cannot check. Where checking is possible, maybe we must check.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I said this teaching before רב כהנא (some say רב כהנא said it before רב שימי), and he answered: Maybe where checking is possible, we must check. Where it is not possible, we cannot check, so we follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from שחיטה is pushed back. It may only work for cases where there is no way to check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שחיטה, the worry is about a hole at the exact spot of the cut, and the cut destroys that spot, so checking it is impossible. That does not prove we may rely on the רוב when we could have checked. So the proof is too narrow for the general rule the גמרא is looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling
And perhaps; it introduces a possible rejection
Possible (here: possible to check)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: I said this teaching
before Rav Kahana,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לָהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שִׁימִי,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Kahana who said it before Rav Shimi,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְדִלְמָא הֵיכָא דְּאֶפְשָׁר – אֶפְשָׁר,
phrases.english: and he said to him: But perhaps where it is possible to check, it is possible,
phrases.notes: He means that if you can check, you must check and you can't just rely on the majority.

phrases.english: and where it is not possible, it is not possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא הֵיכָא דְּאֶפְשָׁר – אֶפְשָׁר, הֵיכָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר – לָא אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the scope of the proof in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the proof to cases where checking is impossible. It does not deny that we follow the רוב there.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שחיטה is a case where checking can't be done, so it cannot teach that we rely on the רוב even when checking is possible.

steps.title: Support from רבי מאיר: even he must eat meat
steps.stepSummary: Support for the distinction: רבי מאיר worries about the minority, yet surely he eats meat. So in a case where checking is impossible, even he relies on the רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you don't say this, then according to רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority, would he really not eat meat?
steps.whatsHappening: The one who pushed back now backs up his distinction by pointing to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר usually does not rely on the רוב, because he worries about the minority. If he still eats slaughtered meat, it must be because a case where checking is impossible is special, and everyone relies on the רוב there. That shows the שחיטה case can't prove the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He worries about the minority (he does not just follow the majority)
For if you don't say so; it introduces proof that the other view leads to something hard to accept
Meat

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
then according to Rabbi Meir, who worries about the minority,
would it really be that he does not eat meat?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּחָיֵישׁ לְמִיעוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the rejection in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction that the רוב is relied on where checking is impossible, even by those who usually worry about the minority.
steps.raayaSupportSource: It is hard to say that רבי מאיר would never eat meat.

steps.title: Considering the reply that רבי מאיר indeed avoids meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a possible reply: maybe רבי מאיר really doesn't eat meat. This sets up the next move.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: yes, that is true (רבי מאיר really doesn't eat meat),
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא raises a possible reply, that רבי מאיר really does not eat meat, and will deal with it in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר truly avoided slaughtered meat, the support in step 19 would collapse. The words 'וכי תימא' signal that the גמרא is about to show this reply doesn't work.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say; it introduces a possible reply that will be answered
Yes, indeed so

phrases.english: And if you would say: indeed so,
phrases.notes: He means: maybe רבי מאיר really doesn't eat meat. The גמרא answers this right after.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible way out of the support in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the hard result (biting the bullet)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed obvious that רבי מאיר must eat meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe רבי מאיר really does avoid meat. The גמרא answers this in the continuation.
